item.title: Kadavu chiefs call for tighter jetty inspections to keep hard drugs out
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua , Pita Toganivalu · 30/07/2026 The chiefs of Kadavu are calling on authorities to ensure that inspections are carried out on cargo and passengers arriving at the Vunisea and Kavala jetties to prevent hard drugs from entering the island.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua , Pita Toganivalu · 30/07/2026

The chiefs of Kadavu are calling on authorities to ensure that inspections are carried out on cargo and passengers arriving at the Vunisea and Kavala jetties to prevent hard drugs from entering the island.

Speaking at the Kadavu Provincial Council meeting at the Civic Centre in Suva, one of the chiefs said hard drugs, including methamphetamine, have already made their way into Kadavu and are being used by young people.

He said cargo and passengers are routinely searched before departing from and upon arriving at the Suva Wharf on vessels travelling to and from Kadavu. However, he claimed that similar inspections are not conducted when cargo is unloaded or when passengers arrive at the jetties in Kadavu.

The chief called on Police to also conduct checks on passengers as they disembark from ships before they travel around the island.

He said action must be taken now to safeguard future generations.

Deputy Divisional Police Commander Central, Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Isireli Ligairi, acknowledged the concern and said Police would take the issue into consideration.

While addressing the Council, ASP Ligairi told the chiefs they may have noticed that Operation Sasamaki is no longer being conducted as frequently because it has been suspended in Kadavu.

He said Police have now shifted their focus to maritime surveillance as part of the fight against drugs.

ASP Ligairi also said several laws are being reviewed, including the Police Act, the Illicit Drugs Control Act, and the Proceeds of Crime Act, to strengthen the country's legal framework in combating drugs.

He added that in the coming months, Police will also examine the income and assets of individuals to ensure their wealth has been acquired through legal means and is not the proceeds of marijuana cultivation or other criminal activity.

item.title: Commonwealth Games: Daunakamakama powers into boxing semi-finals and medal contention
item.description: Team Fiji's medal hopes received a major boost after boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama powered into the semi-finals of the Women's 57kg division with a commanding 4-1 victory over Sri Lanka's Keshani Hansika. On the track, Heleina Young clocked a season-best time of 24.45 seconds to finish sixth in the Women's 200 metres heats, while long-distance specialist Yeshnil Karan also recorded a season best, fi
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji's medal hopes received a major boost after boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama powered into the semi-finals of the Women's 57kg division with a commanding 4-1 victory over Sri Lanka's Keshani Hansika.

On the track, Heleina Young clocked a season-best time of 24.45 seconds to finish sixth in the Women's 200 metres heats, while long-distance specialist Yeshnil Karan also recorded a season best, finishing 12th in the Men's One Mile event in 4 minutes 12.28 seconds.

In the pool, Kelera Mudunasoko placed sixth in the Women's 200 metres Breaststroke with a time of 2 minutes 47.86 seconds.

Team Fiji's men's swimming team also finished seventh in the 4x100 metres Medley Relay, clocking 4 minutes 2.77 seconds.

Meanwhile, it was a tough outing on the bowling greens, with Elizabeth Moceiwai going down 2-0 to Scotland's Sophie McGrouther in the Women's Singles Sectional, while Fiji's Men's Pairs team also lost to New Zealand in their sectional match.

Attention now turns to another busy day of competition for Team Fiji.

Sitiveni Konataci will compete in the Men's Discus Throw F42-44/F61-64 Final from 7.25am this morning.

Later tonight, Elizabeth Moceiwai will resume her Women's Singles Sectional campaign at 7.30pm, before Fiji's Men's Pairs bowling team returns to action in its sectional match at 8.55pm.

In weightlifting, Taniela Tuisuva Rainibogi will take to the platform in the Men's 110kg competition, which gets underway at 8.30pm tonight.

Meanwhile, Australia continues to dominate the medal tally with 35 gold, 18 silver and 29 bronze medals. Canada is second with 13 gold, 11 silver and 13 bronze medals, while England is third with 10 gold, 19 silver and 15 bronze medals.

item.title: Fiji imports processed sugar for manufacturers- Tunabuna
item.description: Fiji imports processed white sugar for manufacturers such as Coca-Cola and other companies, while raw sugar for supermarkets is only imported when there is insufficient locally produced sugar. This was highlighted by Minister for Sugar Tomasi Tunabuna while speaking to fijivillage News, saying this is done particularly when production is low or after a natural disaster.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji imports processed white sugar for manufacturers such as Coca-Cola and other companies, while raw sugar for supermarkets is only imported when there is insufficient locally produced sugar.

This was highlighted by Minister for Sugar Tomasi Tunabuna while speaking to fijivillage News, saying this is done particularly when production is low or after a natural disaster.

Tunabuna says the Fiji Sugar Corporation (FSC) has reported that it has some stock available for supermarkets.

He says Fiji normally imports raw sugar when there is insufficient sugar, especially when production is low or when the country experiences a natural disaster.

Insert:Tunabuna on sugar import 29th July.

The Minister says white sugar, icing sugar and other processed sugars are all imported and are not made from Fiji's brown sugar.

He explains that Fiji produces raw sugar, while processed sugars are imported at all times.

Providing an update on the crushing season, the Minister says the Lautoka and Labasa mills are operating at above 80 percent of their capacity, while the Ba Mill is operating at a little over 60 percent capacity, adding that production is now picking up.

Meanwhile, the Minister also highlights efforts to support diversification among sugarcane farmers.

He says last week he handed over a project to a farming community involved in sugarcane, which can also be used for cultivating other crops.

He says more than 30 rice harvesters have been provided over the past three weeks.

The Minister says they are also looking at increasing the fertiliser subsidy to include other crops so they can continue providing assistance to sugarcane farmers, allowing them to benefit from growing other crops, not just sugarcane.

item.title: Opposition MP Vijay Nath calls for urgent Police action following attacks on taxi drivers in Wainibokasi
item.description: Following the recent increase in robberies and assaults against taxi drivers in Wainibokasi, Opposition MP, Vijay Nath has called the Government and the Police to take immediate and decisive action before the situation deteriorates further. Nath says Police must increase its visibility in crime-prone areas through regular foot patrols, mobile patrols and targeted policing operations, particularly
item.content:encoded:
Following the recent increase in robberies and assaults against taxi drivers in Wainibokasi, Opposition MP, Vijay Nath has called the Government and the Police to take immediate and decisive action before the situation deteriorates further.

Nath says Police must increase its visibility in crime-prone areas through regular foot patrols, mobile patrols and targeted policing operations, particularly around the Nausori Bus Stand, the mini-bus stand and surrounding areas where these incidents have been reported.

He says Police should also strengthen intelligence gathering, engage closely with taxi associations and business owners, and conduct regular operations to identify and apprehend repeat offenders.

Nath says a visible and proactive police presence will not only deter criminal activity but also restore public confidence that Nausori is a safe place to live, work and do business.

The Opposition MP says authorities must also take firm action against intoxicated people behaving aggressively or threatening taxi drivers and members of the public.

He says these attacks are no longer confined to the late hours of the night.

Nath says many drivers are refusing to operate after 7pm because they no longer feel safe.

He says t his is not just a problem for taxi operators and it affects workers trying to get home, students travelling to and from school, families, the elderly, businesses and the wider public who rely on taxis everyday.

Nath adds that when taxi drivers fear for their lives, the entire community suffers.

The Opposition MP says the time for action is now.

Responding to our questions, Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says they are doing their best, in line with the resources and capabilities they have, through ongoing investigations and patrols.

Vusonilawe is urging taxi drivers to always take precautionary measures and, if they are suspicious of their passengers, to drive to the nearest Police Station or Community Post.

He adds that, regarding the installation of CCTV cameras, Police do not have the budget to facilitate CCTV coverage in every corner of a central business district, and they need the public's assistance in addressing the issues raised.

item.title: Urgent appeal for A+ and O+ blood donors to assist Ravneel Lal
item.description: An urgent appeal is being made for A+ and O+ blood donors to help Ravneel Lal, who is currently admitted at Oceania Hospital. People with either of these blood types can go to the Oceania Hospital Reception and inform the receptionist that they are there to donate blood for Ravneel Lal.
item.content:encoded:
An urgent appeal is being made for A+ and O+ blood donors to help Ravneel Lal, who is currently admitted at Oceania Hospital.

People with either of these blood types can go to the Oceania Hospital Reception and inform the receptionist that they are there to donate blood for Ravneel Lal.

Those who are unable to donate are being urged to share the appeal with family, friends, colleagues, community groups, and on social media to help reach more potential donors.
